title: Execution from a sequence of steps
statement: Let $W$ be a word width, $P$ a finite program, $n$ a nonnegative integer, and $c,c'$ configurations consisting of a program counter and an integer-indexed memory of $W$-bit words. Suppose $c$ reaches $c'$ in exactly $n$ steps, each of which continues to another configuration, and the next step from $c'$ halts with Boolean verdict $v$. Then executing $P$ from the program counter and memory of $c$ for $n+1$ steps returns verdict $v$ and the memory of $c'$.
hypotheses_covered: There is an n-step sequence of continuing steps from c to c'
The step from c' halts with verdict v
